The case originated in an application (no. 28045/02) against the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland under Article 34 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (“the Convention”) by a British national, Mr Robert Murray (“the applicant”), on 1 March 2001. The applicant was born in 1949 and lives in Lancashire. His second claim for widows’ benefits was made in July 2000 and was rejected on 11 July 2000 on the ground that he was not entitled to widows’ benefits because he was not a woman. On 2 October 2000 the applicant applied for reconsideration and on 1 November 2000 he was requested to complete another claim form. The applicant did so and his claim was rejected on 20 November 2000. The applicant did not appeal further as he considered or was advised that such a remedy would be bound to fail since no such social security benefits were payable to widowers under United Kingdom law. At the time of his claim the applicant was in receipt of child benefit.
